title: a text multiget's read buffer is copied after it went back to the rbuf cache
live_proof: the fix is an ancestor of the 1.6.45 tag: GitHub compare 1.6.45...7af02b0c87 reports status=behind, behind_by=566; the case reconstructs the pre-fix order of the two lines, which the commit's own diff shows
object: the connection's READ_BUFFER_SIZE read buffer, an object of the thread's rbuf cache (cache.c)
lifetime_ender: do_cache_free, which pushes the buffer on the cache's STAILQ (cache.c:135) and writes the list link into its first pointer-sized bytes; free() is never called
shape: stale object pointer / cache.c reuse / read through the dead pointer
allocator_layer: cache.c object cache over malloc, memcached 1.6.45
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator: cache.c is upstream's file at the 1.6.45 pin through the port's two patches (freestanding shim, object lifetime hooks); the connection, the parser and the thread are reduced to the two lines the fix reorders, plus one prior buffer on the free list so the link read back is a pointer
layer_note: upstream's commit message names the mechanism -- the cache 'can reuse the first 8 bytes as a pointer to the internal freelist' -- and that is the only reason the defect was visible: for years the free list did not touch the buffer. The port's hook sits on that push, which is where the buffer's lifetime ends

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm copies the command after the buffer was pushed on the free list, so the copy's first bytes are the STAILQ link and differ from the command; the fixed arm copies first and the bytes are intact
native-fix-differential.note: unit_reissued is 1 in BOTH arms by design -- the next connection's cache_alloc pops the buffer either way; the arms differ only in whether the copy read it after the push

spatial.oracle: the sequence completes: report.completed == 1, no fault, the case marker printed
spatial.role: control for sublet: same binary and guest, one difference. An object keeps the alias it was carved with, so the freed buffer is readable and the copy proceeds -- with the link in it, as upstream saw

native-detect.requires: the buffer never reaches free(), so ASan has no event at the push; it would see the reuse only as an ordinary live object
native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -g; port library with the same sanitizer). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 67108864` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 67108864` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (3ef5169ae90b); the arm was previously 'not written'.
native-detect.measured: 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-native-asan-stock-malloc/run-asan.txt: SILENT -- the defect reproduced (VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED) and ASan printed nothing; built with MCP_STOCK_MALLOC=ON (each page and cache.c object its own malloc, as upstream); both controls reported in the same run

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host: the sequence COMPLETES. exit=0, completed=1, object_reuses=1, chunk_reuses=0. Not caught. The reuse counters are the point: the storage really was handed back out, which is the situation revocation would have to catch if the memory reached free(). It does not -- cache.c keeps it on its own STAILQ and slabs.c returns it to the page, so libc's quarantine never holds it. EVIDENCE COMMITTED 2026-10-06: results/20261006-cheribsd/. Both controls are in that bundle -- the revocation control FAULTED with addr == pc == the independently resolved expectation (0x101e42), proving the revoker sweeps in this guest AND attributing the fault; and a NEGATIVE CONTROL run on the same vehicle makes all 8 case oracles FAIL while the three platform controls still pass, so none of these completions is vacuous. The image hash is byte-identical to the vehicle the ffmpeg readings of the same day used, so the two programs' columns are comparable. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-cheribsd-fixed-buggy/ (R1): buggy and FIXED arms, same program, same boot, both complete; the revocation control faulted at its labelled load in that boot.
cheribsd-revocation.control: the control fired in the SAME boot: revocation-control exit=162 signal=34 (SIGPROT) si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) with pc == the address the supervisor resolved independently (0x101e42). The platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds passed in the same run.

note: damage is the copied command differing from what was read: natively the first 8 bytes become the free list's link, in a domain the first 16. Upstream reported an unhelpful ERROR to the client; this records the byte-level cause of it
nested_why: memcached's cache.c object cache carved the object out of memory it owns -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NESTED.
